name.description: The word the caller uses for this agent: its name in the caller's workspace, another workspace's lead by that workspace's name, any other agent as name (workspace).

reports_to.description: The key of the agent or person it reports to; null for none.

agent.description: The agent the proposal is about, as the card heads it `<kind> <agent>`. For a bundle: `<N> changes`, not an agent's name.

title.description: One line, the card's head: `<kind> <agent>`; a bundle's is `bundle <N> changes`. Text from agents' names; draw as text.

diff.description: What approving does, in words, one change per line. Not a unified diff.

state.description: open: waits for the founder. applying: approved by the founder and held until each agent in `waiting_on` ends its turn; the daemon then closes those sessions, applies the change and restarts each agent that stays; it turns approved once the change is applied (an agent that stays and does not start at once is `follow_up`, not a failure), or apply_failed when the change itself fails; `settled` stays null and the founder is offered no action meanwhile. approved: decided and applied. rejected. apply_failed: approved by the founder but not applied (the apply failed, or never ran): still the founder's move, and proposal.decide approve again applies it. withdrawn: taken back by its author or the founder. An open set: a client draws a word it does not know as text, offers no action on it and does not count it. See proposal.list for the proposal file's own states.

waiting_on.description: Set only while state is applying: the agents whose running turn the change waits on, by their names before the change. A card names them.

waiting_since.description: Set only while state is applying: when the proposal turned applying. With `waiting_on` it tells the card since when and why it waits (those agents' turns are running); proposal.apply_now ends the wait.

state.description: waiting: the start is put off for machine load and the daemon makes it by itself when the load drops; the card shows no retry. failed: the start failed for another reason and only the founder's Start now (agent.force_start) retries it. An open set: draw a word you do not know as text.

text.description: Why, from the daemon (the held limit or the failure), one line.

follow_up.description: Set on an approved proposal whose change is applied but an agent it renamed is not running yet. Absent when the change needs no start or the start went through; it is removed when the start succeeds. The change is applied either way: a client never draws it as not applied or offers approve again.

subject.description: Digest of what the proposal changes as drawn; proposal.decide's approve hands it back.

requested_by.description: Who asked: an agent's key, or the person's for the founder's own change (a retire held for a running session, say); a client draws a person key as the person, never as an agent. Text from the daemon's record; optional.

reason.description: Why it asks, as the agent wrote it. Text only, from an agent: a client draws it as plain text, never as markup, and drops control characters. Optional.

note.description: The founder's note on the decision (why it was rejected, say), as proposal.decide took it. Absent when the founder gave none or it is still open.

asked.description: The fields the proposal asks for (vendor, model, effort, team, repo, to, then each `set <key>`). Every value is text from an agent (same rule as `reason`); optional, and a key it did not ask for is absent. Absent for kind bundle: its `diff` carries the changes. members, repos, relation, response and context texts are in `diff` only.

sets.description: `set <key>`: each agent setting asked for, key to value.

oneOf.description: Why the change did not go through; set when state is apply_failed and an apply ran and failed, else null. Text only; the daemon cuts it at 400 characters. Optional.
When it was decided, withdrawn or its apply failed; null while open. Optional.

kind.description: What the proposal does: add, retire, rename, team, settings, context, schedule, run (a shell command the founder runs with the approve) or bundle (several changes decided once). An open set: a client draws a word it does not know as text.

run.description: Kind run only: the command and, once the approve started it, its run. The run's output goes to the proposing agent: a card says so before the press.

command.description: The command in full, as it will run; text from an agent: draw it as text, never cut.

cwd.description: The absolute folder it runs in.

risks.description: Hints for reading, from the text alone: delete, overwrite, network, outside, outside_home, privilege. Never a gate, and none is not safe. An open set: draw a word you do not know as text.

state.description: Absent until the approve started it; then running, done (exit 0), failed (another exit) or stopped (its window closed first), as CommandRun.state. An open set.

terminal.description: The run's window, as terminal.attach takes it; set once started.

exit.description: The exit status once done or failed.

ProposalArgs.description: What the proposal changes, by kind (hl propose). Every kind needs name.

name.description: The agent the proposal is about (the new agent's name for add; a team's manager for team).

members.description: team: each a suffix (`sea` is `name.sea`) or a full name.

sets.description: settings: agent setting keys as AgentSettingValues names them. context: whole new file texts keyed `ROLE.md` or `base.md`; empty text or control characters other than tab and newline is bad_request.

items.description: A step: kind (add, retire, rename, team, context) and the other fields of this type, name included.

changes.description: bundle: the steps, at most 40, each judged against the roster the earlier ones leave. name is then ignored (send the count, `3 changes`).

action.description: schedule: add a schedule to `name`, edit one of its (give was_cron for which; cron and message are then the new ones, a missing one stays), or remove one (was_cron).

cron.description: schedule add, edit: five cron fields; it may not fire more than once an hour (bad_request).

message.description: schedule add, edit: the text typed at the agent each time, at most 1000 characters.

was_cron.description: schedule edit, remove: the cron of the existing schedule.

was_message.description: schedule edit, remove: its message, when two of the agent's schedules share the cron.

command.description: run: the shell command the founder's approve runs in a terminal window, 1 to 4000 characters, no NUL. One string, run by the window's shell: a pipeline or `&&` is one proposal.

cwd.description: run: the folder it runs in; it must be a directory when proposed. A relative one is taken from the agent's worktree; kept absolute.

error.description: Why the agent's `schedules` value cannot be read.

display_name.description: What the app shows for the person.

handle.description: The word other people address them by in team mode; null in personal mode.

folder.description: The project folder its agents' worktrees are made from.

added_folders.description: Further folders its agents may read and write.

lead.description: The key of its lead agent; null before it has one.

methods.name: proposal.propose
methods.summary: Propose a roster change; the founder decides (hl propose add, retire, rename, team, settings, context, schedule, run (a shell command the founder's approve runs in a terminal window; at most 5 open per agent, the sixth refused), and diff, which is kind bundle: args.changes lists several changes decided once and applied together or not at all).

methods.name: proposal.withdraw
methods.summary: Take back an undecided proposal: its author's own, or any for the founder; another agent is refused (gate role).

methods.name: trust.propose
methods.summary: Propose declaring a folder Handline may answer Claude's trust prompt in (hl trust add); the founder's own call declares it.
methods.description: Called by an agent it raises a decision for the founder, `why` required, and answers the proposal's id; called by the founder it declares the root directly, `why` optional (default `added by the founder`), and answers no proposal. A root already inside a declared one, a missing why or a decision that could not be raised is refused with the store's words. A paired device is refused, gate role. `root` must be an absolute path (bad_request, field `root`): the daemon would read a relative one, or `~`, against its own folder and home, so the client resolves it against its own.

methods.name: trust.list
methods.summary: Declared trust roots, and with proposals the proposals (hl trust list, hl trust proposals).

request.description: The decision request that asked the founder.

proposals.description: Empty unless `proposals` is true. State is the store's word (proposed, applied, rejected...).

added_by.description: An agent's key, or a person's.

declared.description: The same roots as `roots`, in the same order, with why and who added each.

methods.name: trust.remove
methods.summary: Drop a declared root (hl trust remove); needs no approval.
methods.description: The founder's: the declared roots live in the protected store, which an agent session cannot write, so an agent calling `hl trust remove` is refused today and by this method (gate role). A root that is not declared is not_found. `root` must be an absolute path, as for trust.propose (bad_request, field `root`).

methods.name: people.list
methods.summary: Every person, so a client writes out a person key by name.

methods.name: workspaces.list
methods.summary: Every workspace, so a client writes out a workspace key by name and groups agents by it.

methods.name: workspace.create
methods.summary: Make a workspace on the top of the git checkout folder is in, with its lead (reporting to the owner, its rules seeded), and start the lead: one operation, answered as agent.create's. Refused before any operation starts: a folder in no checkout (gate not_git), a missing one (not_found, what folder), a name a workspace has (gate state). Owner only; an agent proposes a team instead.
methods.description: The operation has kind workspace.create and its agent is the workspace's name (its lead); its steps and result are agent.create's. A folder another workspace's shares, or a name the rules refuse, fails it with the reason. A start that fails leaves the workspace and its lead registered, so its name is in use: start the lead with session.start (hl wake), or remove it with workspace.delete.

schema.description: The workspace's name: lowercase letters, digits and -, 1 to 32 long, starting with a letter, used by no workspace and no person's handle. A dot or a slash is bad_request, field name.
The project folder, an absolute path (~ is the home folder).

methods.name: workspace.set
methods.summary: Rename a workspace: its name is the one thing this changes. Keys never change; the dotted form of each agent's name (workspace.agent) follows the new name, and the old one no longer resolves. Refused (gate state) while one of its agents has a session running, while an open proposal names one by its dotted name, or for a name the rules refuse or a workspace or person's handle has. The same name is no change. Owner only.

schema.description: The workspace's key (w3) or its name, as workspaces.list gives them. An unknown one is not_found, what workspace.
The new name: lowercase letters, digits and -, 1 to 32 long, starting with a letter.

methods.name: workspace.delete
methods.summary: Delete a workspace: each of its agents is retired as agent.retire retires one, its lead last, and the workspace goes with the lead. The project folder is never touched. Nothing is done when any agent has a session running or an agent of another workspace under it (gate state), a worktree holds work with no worktree answer (gate dirty, every agent's in worktrees), or a worktree cannot go (gate worktree). While it runs, agent.create and the session methods in the workspace are refused (gate state), and it is refused while one of them is under way. Git or the disk failing part way puts back every retire before it, but not a worktree already removed; the call is refused (gate state) naming the step. Owner only.

schema.description: The workspace's key (w3) or its name, as workspaces.list gives them. An unknown one is not_found, what workspace.

The founder's answer for every worktree of the workspace's agents that holds work, as agent.retire's save and force. keep, which would keep an agent, is bad_request, field worktree, as is any other word.

methods.name: team.get
methods.summary: The caller's team: the agents of its workspace (all of them for a person outside every workspace folder, as the app is), the people, and the other workspaces. Each name is the word the caller uses for that key.

name.description: The word the caller uses for this person: human for its owner or itself, else the handle or display name.

workspaces.description: The workspaces other than the caller's own.

lead.description: Its lead agent's key, which receives what is sent to the workspace.

methods.name: proposal.list
methods.summary: proposals with their diff: what waits for the founder, and what settled recently.

schema.description: Only the proposals in that state; without it, the list below.

methods.description: Without `state`: every proposal that waits (open, applying, and apply_failed until it is decided again) and every settled one (approved, rejected, withdrawn) from the last 7 days, at most 50 of those. Order: the waiting ones first, oldest `created` first; then the settled ones, newest `settled` first. A client counts the dot from `open` and `apply_failed`, never from `applying`. With `state`, only that state, in the same order, and no 7-day or 50 bound. A proposal whose requested_by is human (the founder's own change) is listed as any other, so a held one shows while it waits. The proposal file's states map as: proposed = open; approved = apply_failed (it holds the founder's approval and the change is not applied: `error` is set when an apply ran and failed, null when it never ran, e.g. a crash between the two); applied = approved; rejected = rejected; withdrawn = withdrawn; enacting and failed are never listed.

methods.name: proposal.decide
methods.summary: Approve or reject a proposal; approving an apply_failed one applies it again. The call answers only with the outcome. Approving a change to an agent with a session running holds it (the proposal turns applying) and the call waits until those turns end and the change is applied, then answers what was done, or the refusal; other calls on the connection are answered meanwhile. Past 10 minutes the held change is dropped (withdrawn), nothing is changed and the call is refused (gate state). Refused with gate proposal_changed or proposal_settled, carrying the proposal as it is; an applying proposal is refused proposal_settled.

params.name: subject
params.description: Required for approve: the proposal's `subject` from proposal.list. Refused if the proposal changed since.

methods.name: proposal.apply_now
methods.summary: Apply a waiting proposal now: for an applying proposal, interrupt the turn of each agent in `waiting_on` (as session.interrupt does), then close the session, apply the change and restart the renamed agent at the next tick, without waiting for the turn to end. The call answers once the change is applied, with what was done, or the refusal; past 10 minutes the held change is dropped (withdrawn) and the call is refused (gate state). Refused with gate proposal_settled, carrying the proposal as it is, unless the proposal is applying. Works for every kind a running session can hold: rename, retire, context, link, settings.

methods.name: proposal.stop
methods.summary: The founder stops the running command of an approved run proposal: its window is closed and the run ends stopped; the proposing agent is told. Refused (gate role) for anyone else, and (gate state) when the proposal is not kind run, its command is not running, or its window is no longer the command's.

methods.name: schedules.list

errors.description: Present only when an agent's `schedules` value cannot be read: that agent, and why.

methods.description: An agent whose `schedules` value is bad is listed in `errors` (target and the error text), not shown as an agent with no schedules.
